message: The accumulator takes the dtype of x and is updated in-place, so integer x with float coefficients fails the same_kind cast (or truncates) instead of promoting like numpy.polyval.
dpnp.asarray(x) allocates a scalar x on the default device/queue, ignoring exec_q and usm_type from get_usm_allocations, so p on another queue breaks compute follows data.
Evaluating each term with x ** (n - 1 - i) instead of Horner's scheme is less accurate, overflows earlier for large degree, and costs O(n^2) multiplications.
Coefficients with ndim > 1 are silently flattened with ravel instead of being rejected or handled like NumPy, producing a wrong-degree polynomial.
Leftover debug print writes to stdout on every call; remove it.
The out parameter is documented and accepted but ignored (never written or validated), and numpy.polyval has no out argument.
The test compares dpnp.polyval against itself instead of numpy.polyval as reference, so it can never fail; integer/mixed dtype, scalar and device cases are untested.
